===Foreman's Log #1===
{{transcript|text=
<nowiki>========================</nowiki>
FOREMAN'S LOG - ENTRY #1
<nowiki>========================</nowiki>

Raided the cathedral this morning to hardly any resistance. The Unioners' little "safehouse" was full of weak and sickly civilians. They were counting on the Trench to protect them. But thanks to that new tracker, our whole group got through the radpits without a hitch.

We've got rotating guards on the prisoners while we build a pen for them. I keep hearing them praying. They don't know yet that no god can save them from what I have planned.
}}

===Foreman's Log #2===
{{transcript|text= <nowiki>========================</nowiki>
FOREMAN'S LOG - ENTRY #2
<nowiki>========================</nowiki>

We drove back the trogs and started building cages underground. But the beasts just keep crawling out of new holes. I'm starting to think we leave them be, make for a little extra security down there... and a convenient way to dispose of underlings who are more of a pain than they're worth. It's not like I ever need to go down there. I'm the god of this temple now. 

That's right. I'm in charge here. I think they're all due for another reminder of that.
}}

===Foreman's Log #3===
{{transcript|text= <nowiki>========================</nowiki>
FOREMAN'S LOG - ENTRY #3
<nowiki>========================</nowiki>

Everything's set up just the way I like it. Pain and punishment rule this house. We're bringing in new prisoners every day and shaping them up for labor under the Fanatics. They can do our dirty work. Build our bases, gather our supplies, act as body shields. The possibilities are endless if you break them just right.

A few of my lieutenants have gone missing, the tracker among them. He's been more quiet than usual lately, and that's saying a lot. It's a loss, but who cares. There's more where that came from. The rest of those pathetic louts probably got dragged away by trogs.
}}

===Foreman's Log #4===
{{transcript|text= <nowiki>========================</nowiki>
FOREMAN'S LOG - ENTRY #4
<nowiki>========================</nowiki>

We ousted that asshole! Fed him to the trogs! It's a new dawn for the Sanctum now!

Order won't last long if we don't appoint a new Foreman soon. We're holding a crucible tomorrow. One prisoner to each lieutenant. Whoever gets the best screams rules the Sanctum!
}}

'''I'm getting out of this town''' is a [[Fallout 76 notes|paper note]] {{In|FO76TP}}.

==Location==
The note can be found in [[the Penn]] of the [[Industrial]] section of [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|The Pitt]] during [[Union Dues]]. It is on a desk in an apartment next to a radio.

==Transcript==
{{Transcript|text=
I saw it, [[Marnie]]. One of those things. I know you don't believe me, but they aren't a myth. They're real. They're stalking us, waiting in the shadows... waiting to pounce.
I'm outta here. Don't know where to, but I can't take it anymore. The [[Radiation|rads]] alone should have done it for me, or the [[Fanatics]], but I tried to hold on, for you. Well there's no more holdin' on.
Maybe out west it's not so bad. Never thought of moving to [[Topeka]] before, but hell, it can't be any worse than up here. I'd ask you to come with me, but I know what you'll say, so I won't wait up. Maybe someday we'll meet again, out on the plains or somewhere altogether different. I do hope that's the case.
Until then, don't get eaten.
[[Ken (Expeditions: The Pitt)|Ken]]
}}

PARTY A acknowledges that this contract obliges them to use force for the interests of PARTY B. '''Haven terminal entries ''' are found on [[Sandra Kundanika|Sandra]]'s research terminal on the top level of [[Haven]] in the ''[[Fallout 3]]'' [[Fallout 3 add-ons|add-on]] ''[[The Pitt (add-on)|The Pitt]]''. ==Research terminal== {{Transcript|text= 
**********************************
*    PITT BIORESEARCH STATION    *
*  KRAG-JENSEN PROTOCOLS LOADED  *
**********************************
}} ===Baby Monitor=== {{Transcript|text= > Baby Status: Healthy and Well }} ===Trog Studies=== {{Transcript|text= [[Troglodyte Degeneration Contagion]] Research by Dr. [[Sandra Kundanika]] An epidemic of the environs around [[The Pitt (Fallout 3)|the Pitt]], which I have named Troglitic Degeneration Contagion (or simply "TDC") appears to be the result of intensely concentrated radiation, but the unique toxins and pollutants in the Pitt cause it to be far more pervasive. Anyone living in TDC-active areas experience skin lesions after a few weeks of exposure, which can clear up after a month or more away from infected areas. For many healthy adults, this is the full extent of the effect. TDC also seems to interact with brain chemistry in a manner that produces a number of [[Wildmen|psychological effects]], even if the subject remains physically healthy. I'll need to recover more information about psychosis before attempting to enumerate those effects. Approximately 20% of adults will progress further, losing higher reasoning and motor skills over the course of years, until they have degenerated into a bestial "[[Trog (The Pitt)|Trog]]". No subjects have ever been recovered from full degeneration, although wishful rumors persist of Trog retaining memories and recognizing the faces of loved ones. More tragic, however, is the fact that children born in TDC-active areas have a (virtually) 100% degeneration rate, often becoming feral within weeks of birth. }} ===Cure Research=== {{small|Adds [[Cure research]] to the player character's inventory.}} {{Transcript|text= Cure Development Progress Research by Dr. Sandra Kundanika Observational tests on isolated samples suggest the subject has a natural adaptive immunity to the so called "trog [[Radiation#Mutations|mutation]]." Furthermore, it appears that this immunity carries on to other forms of [[radiation]]-induced diseases - from radiation sickness to larger mutations such as the all-too-common development of [[Mutated toe|a sixth toe]]. Attempts to isolate these effects have been slow going, due in part to the delicate nature of testing. Prospects exist for duplication, but the unique and delicate nature of [[Marie (The Pitt)|the subject]] requires utmost care in testing. }} [[Category:The Pitt terminal entries]] [[de:Haven Terminaleinträge]] [[es:Entradas de terminales del Refugio]] [[fr:Entrées de terminal de Haven]] [[ru:Исследовательский компьютер]]

{{DLC ID|00ab9a}} (diary 4) }} '''Ashur's diary''' is a series of [[The Pitt holotapes|holotape]]s in the ''[[Fallout 3]]'' [[Fallout 3 add-ons|add-on]] ''[[The Pitt (add-on)|The Pitt]]''. ==Locations== The tapes are found in a locked [[Safe (Fallout 3)|safe]] in Ashur's room in [[Haven]] and contain messages from [[Ishmael Ashur]] to his daughter [[Marie (The Pitt)|Marie]]. Opening the safe, with or without [[Fallout 3 keys#Ashur's key|Ashur's key]], and taking them will count as stealing, thus result in negative [[Karma (Fallout 3)|Karma]]. ==Transcripts== The script notes are: "Hesitates briefly at first, but gets into his stride, basically making a "video diary" for his newborn daughter, in case something happens to him." ===Diary 1: To Marie=== [[File:FO3TP Ashur Diary1ToMarie.ogg|center]] {{Transcript|text= {{Tooltip|Test, one, two. Looks like this thing's on. Marie, if you're there, this is your father speaking: Ishmael Ashur, sometimes called Lord of The Pitt.|Hesitates briefly at first, but gets into his stride, basically making a "video diary" for his newborn daughter, in case something happens to him.}} Now, I hope you're hearing this ten years from now, sitting on my knee safe and sound. Right about now, I bet I'm looking pretty silly. But things don't always work out the way we'd like. There are a lot of risks, including what your mother would do if she heard me talking like this. And I'm not about to risk leaving you alone without knowing where you came from. These tapes are for you, so you can know who your father really was. }} ===Diary 2: The Scourge=== [[File:FO3TP Ashur Diary2TheScourge.ogg|center]] {{Transcript|text= Marie, the first thing you need to know is that I wasn't always the Lord of [[The Pitt (Fallout 3)|The Pitt]]. Long before I was a king, I was a scholar and a soldier. In fact, I was in the [[Brotherhood of Steel]]. You've probably heard about them. But you may not have heard what we did to this city: [[the Scourge]]. When we came here, The Pitt was just a breeding ground for [[Trog (The Pitt)|Trogs]], [[Cannibalism|cannibals]], and worse. Commander had us torch the place and take what we could. The Pitt had useful [[technology]], but it was suicide to stay here. So when an explosion left me buried in [[the Mill]], my brothers were sure I was dead. I don't blame them for leaving. I probably would have. We thought nothing could live in The Pitt. We were wrong. }} ===Diary 3: The Mill=== [[File:FO3TP Ashur Diary3TheMill.ogg|center]] {{Transcript|text= Marie, you know those fights in the Mill's arena? Well, its first fight was when I woke up to someone pulling me out from a pile of rubble. At first I thought it was my brothers pulling me to safety. Instead, it was a [[Scavenger (Fallout 3)|scavenger]] trying to steal [[Ashur's power armor|my armor]]. She didn't get it. But I learned she had a whole family of scavengers. They'd make raids into the city for gear from the Mill. And that gave me an idea. This was the only working steel mill we'd ever seen. In a world of leftovers, it was a chance to build again. And that was worth any price. The scavengers saw me as a god, so along with my Brotherhood know-how, it was easy to set up the basics. We started to build a city. }} ===Diary 4: The Cure=== [[File:FO3TP Ashur Diary4TheCure.ogg|center]] {{Transcript|text= As word of a new settlement got out, the city started growing, and fast. When [[Raiders]] attacked, I'd kill the leader and recruit the rest. I had to. [[Troglodyte Degeneration Contagion|The city's disease]] meant we couldn't have [[child]]ren, so recruiting was the only way to grow. And as we grew, the Mill needed more workers. And, yes, that meant recruiting workers by force. I'm not proud of it, but it's the only way to keep the city supplied and armed. But it was always a temporary solution, until our best scientist found a way to cure the city's epidemic. [[Sandra Kundanika|Sandra]] and I worked on it day and night. {{Tooltip|And after one, particularly late night of work, we were blessed with a cure. It's the cure inside you, Marie.|Euphemism on "particularly late night of work" - when Marie was conceived}} Even now, we're doing everything we can to figure out how to share your gift with the city - while keeping you safe, of course! So by the time you're old enough to hear this, you'll already be a hero. Congratulations, Marie. You've already saved us all. I knew you would. }} {{Navbox holotapes FO3}} [[Category:The Pitt holotapes]] [[de:Ashurs Tagebuch]] [[es:Diario de Ashur]] [[fr:Journaux d'Ashur]] [[ru:Записи Ашура]]

'''Scavenger's journal''' is a [[Fallout 76 notes|paper note]] {{In|FO76TP}}.

==Location==
The note can be found on a table in the Shipping Warehouse area in [[The Foundry]] in [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|The Pitt]], during [[Union Dues]].

==Transcript==
{{Transcript|text=

Diary dearest,
Roaming the streets of [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|Pittsburgh]] on yesterday eve was I, quite enjoying the calming crackle of gunfire (pop, pop-pop-pop) when lo did I behold a sight so unexpected that it startled me more than a [[Pittsburgh Union|Union]] ambush! In the darkest corner of the backest alleyway did I spy a large crate of enemy rations, wholly unguarded among the half-eaten corpses of our foe!

"Surely a trap," I pondered to myself, yet cautiously I approached. I could not let this opportunity escape! After much prodding from afar I determined that this boon was unlikely to explode upon immediate contact. Nor did mine senses detect the slightest hint of an ambush lying in wait.

I alighted with my prize, back to [[the Foundry]] from whence I came. But a cloud still hangs above mine head. Forsooth, perhaps this eminent stash only spells disaster when it is opened? The thought gnaws at me. I cannot risk disaster at so late a stage!
I have hidden yonder cache away among the blast furnaces, where it will be safe from prying eyes until I can determine a method of attack.
}}

'''The Old Guard, Vol 14: Ch 2''' is a [[Wastelanders notes|paper note]] in the ''[[Fallout 76]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]] ''[[Wastelanders]]'', written by [[Fred Radcliff|Sergeant Radcliff]].

==Location==
The note can be found in [[Founder's Hall]], on a table in the southernmost cabin. It is only available after [[Duty Calls]].

==Transcript==
{{Transcript|text=
'''The Old Guard'''

''Volume 14: Chapter 2''

Ok, where was I? Right ... when I first signed up, it was an all hands situation. We'd just gone to [[Sino-American War|war]]. I was a dumb kid like all the others ... but [[Oliver Fields|Fields]] watched my back, made sure my armor was in good repair. I only lost one toe to frostbite, compared to [[Thompson (Wastelanders)|Thompson's]] three. So when the shit hit the fan in [[The Pitt (Fallout 3)|Pittsburgh]], you know I was expecting him to be all over saving those civvies we ran across. I never expected he'd blow his knee out just getting to his armor. Never expected he'd get shot.
Thompson had [[Angel (Wastelanders)|Angel]] and [[Odysseus]] protect him when he went down or he'd be dead now, but it was rough to see. Angel lost her front leg from that. I found myself thinking, you know ... we're all getting so old, our last suit of armor's all beat to shit. Even if we make it out of this alright, he's going to be wearing the rig again for a while just to take the weight off his knee. Why shouldn't we just join those civvies, finally retire, just forget the past like all the other old jerks out there who lived through it.
That night, we finally heard the broadcast again. It made everything feel a little less final. Our [[Fusion core (Fallout 76)|cores]] would run out soon, the armor was basically done for, but there were [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 76)|other ex-military folks]] still out there in [[Appalachia]]. We figured you know, what's one more winter of this misery? It's only September. We're not that far away, if we can avoid the hot zones. Won't take that long, we'll just take some time for Fields to heal up. 
We held on to the hope of meeting those troops for a long time after the last broadcast. Maybe they had an equipment failure. Maybe they weren't dead. Or I dunno, maybe if they were dead, then they at least knew where other remnants of the [[United States Armed Forces|military]] were hiding out. Lots of maybes. ...
}}

==Behind the scenes==
[[Oliver Fields|Captain Fields]], [[Thompson (Wastelanders)|Sergeant Thompson]], [[Fred Radcliff|Sergeant Radcliff]], [[Lucky (Wastelanders)|Private Lucky]], [[Odysseus]], and [[Angel (Wastelanders)|Angel]] are all identified as members of [[The Old Guard, Vol 14: Ch 2|The Old Guard]]. Their presence is a nod to the real-world [https://oldguard.mdw.army.mil/specialty-platoons/k9-detachment 947th Military Police Detachment], part of the U.S. Army’s 4th Battalion, 3d U.S. Infantry Regiment, otherwise known as The Old Guard. This unit has the second largest Military Working Dog detachment in the continental United States and works closely with the U.S. Secret Service, identical to their role in ''[[Fallout 76]].''

'''The Hellcats' new assignment''' is a [[Fallout 76 notes|paper note]] {{In|FO76TP}}.

==Location==
The note can be found in the [[Fanatics]] labor yard in [[the Trench]] in [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|The Pitt]], during [[From Ashes to Fire]]. It is on a table in the locked area with the crafting workbenches.

==Transcript==
{{Transcript|text=
Survival comes first, and mercenary work is a great way to stay off the losing side. But that's not gonna stop me from complaining about how these [[Fanatics]] do things.

They hired us on a few weeks ago. Seems they needed some extra guns to finish securing their hold on [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]]. But this just looks like chaos and tyranny more than any type of control. They have us storm into [[Pittsburgh Union|Union]] bases, kill everyone in sight, and then move on to the next without so much as stopping to loot the wreckage. Last time, one of those assholes accidentally shot [[Hoffman (Expeditions: The Pitt)|Hoffman]] in the leg during the assault. Couldn't tell friend from foe.

There's been talk of leaving this place after our stint with the Fanatics is done, finding work somewhere we could actually sleep at night. It wouldn't be a bad call. 

But me? I prefer a known enemy, and I've known the Pitt all my life.

-[[A. Rhoades]], [[Hellcat Company|Hellcat Mercenary Company]]
}}

'''Elsie's journal''' is a [[Wastelanders notes|paper note]] in the ''[[Fallout 76]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]] ''[[Wastelanders]]''. It was written by [[Elsie Taylor]].

==Location==
The note can be found in the Taylors' home at [[Foundation]], on a kitchen counter. It cannot be picked up.

==Transcript==
{{Transcript|text=
I'm not much of a writer, but Derrick won't do it, so I have to. Davie deserves to have it written down.

[[Derrick Taylor|Derrick]] and [[Elsie Taylor|I]] met in [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]]. He was stuck building things for them. I was one of [[Pitt raiders (faction)|their]] enforcers. I was already hating that job and he was hating his. We agreed we both hated the Pitt. But it wasn't until [[Davie Taylor|Davie]] came along that we decided to do something about it.

Derrick hates guns, but he used one that day. Never hit anything he was aiming at. I had to put eight of them down to get us out of there. I came out with a cracked rib and a bullet graze on my scalp. I'm proud to say that Derrick never got a scratch.

After I ambushed the hunting party they sent after us, they must have decided we weren't worth the pain. Never saw another Pitt raider.

Now we're here in [[Foundation]]. We were always on the move before. Never staying anywhere more than a week. That's no way to raise a child. Foundation has changed all that. It's changed all that for you, Davie.
}}

WHY WE FIGHT

When you feel that the walls are closing in around you, remember WHY WE FIGHT. Look to the left and right at your fellow human being, working in unison to achieve our goal of a peaceful tomorrow for [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|Pittsburgh]]. Look out the window at the chaos below. '''A farewell to Pittsburgh''' is a [[Fallout 76 notes|paper note]] {{In|FO76TP}}.

==Location==
The note can be found in the [[Industrial]] section of [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|The Pitt]], on the ground next to a [[Ning|Hellcat mercenary corpse]] in a booby-trapped store during [[Union Dues]].

==Transcript==
{{Transcript|text=
Last chronicle of [[Ning|Sgt. Ning]], [[Hellcat Company]] -- or what's left of it, anyway.

We've spent a long time in [[The Pitt (Fallout 76)|the Pitt]]. The wars among its occupants have been incessant, but all that is finally drawing to a close. Not much left in the way of resistance, anymore. The [[Fanatics]] own damn near everything. Only the [[Pittsburgh Union|Union]] remains... Until this monolith falls apart and it starts all over again.

We made the right choice becoming mercenaries, I still believe that. Fought on every which side and made a killing doing it. We came out on top, and now we should get the hell out before the Fanatics turn on us, too.

Some of the others may have doubts, given the casualties we've sustained, and I get that. Has to be that half of us are gone now, from when I started. Maybe more, hard to keep count. But that's behind us now. I have no interest in sticking around to find out what "peace time" means for these raiders. I'm moving on to greener pastures.

This world needs its killers, or its defenders, or whatever you'll pay me to be. Have to be other towns out there just as fucked as we were by the war and the bombs and everything that goes with it. I hear [[Kit]]'s taking some of the others and heading south, but that sounds weak... [[Appalachia]] is soft, no bombs there, no challenge.

No, I'll go elsewhere. See what trouble I can get into. Gets my blood pumping just thinking about it.
}}
